findings.body: The SMS endpoint deletes the unrelated email, WhatsApp, or other-method reminder before processing SMS reminders.
findings.failure_mode: A method-specific cleanup job performs cross-method destructive database deletion.
findings.impact: The SMS endpoint deletes the unrelated email, WhatsApp, or other-method reminder before processing SMS reminders.
findings.root_cause: The new retry condition is a top-level OR branch rather than being constrained by method: WorkflowMethods.SMS.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the retry predicate under the SMS method constraint, for example by using method: WorkflowMethods.SMS together with an OR containing the past-date and retry-count conditions.
findings.title: Retry cleanup can delete reminders from other delivery methods
findings.trigger: The SMS cron runs while a WorkflowReminder for another method has retryCount greater than 1, whether from another retrying producer or existing database state.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 31-43 show the deleteMany OR clause where the second branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no method constraint. This will delete any WorkflowReminder (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, etc.) with retryCount > 1, not just SMS reminders. The trigger is realistic (any reminder with retryCount > 1 exists when SMS cron runs) and impact is data loss for non-SMS reminders.

pr.body:
## What does this PR do?

Right now when SMS fails to send because of whatever reason (e.g. invalid phone number), we are trying to keep scheduling it in our corn job until the date is reached. This PR introduces a retry count, after scheduling failed twice we delete the workflow reminder.
pr.title: fix: add retryCount to workflowReminder

raw_findings.body: The SMS endpoint deletes the unrelated email, WhatsApp, or other-method reminder before processing SMS reminders.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A method-specific cleanup job performs cross-method destructive database deletion.
raw_findings.impact: The SMS endpoint deletes the unrelated email, WhatsApp, or other-method reminder before processing SMS reminders.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new retry condition is a top-level OR branch rather than being constrained by method: WorkflowMethods.SMS.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Keep the retry predicate under the SMS method constraint, for example by using method: WorkflowMethods.SMS together with an OR containing the past-date and retry-count conditions.
raw_findings.title: Retry cleanup can delete reminders from other delivery methods
raw_findings.trigger: The SMS cron runs while a WorkflowReminder for another method has retryCount greater than 1, whether from another retrying producer or existing database state.

raw_findings.body: Both workers write the same stale count plus one, so a failure is lost and the reminder can remain past the intended two-failure limit.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Concurrent cron workers overwrite each other's retry state, making retry-based cleanup nondeterministic.
raw_findings.impact: Both workers write the same stale count plus one, so a failure is lost and the reminder can remain past the intended two-failure limit.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch performs a read-modify-write using retryCount copied into the initial findMany result.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use Prisma's atomic retryCount increment operation at both update sites, and retain any needed predicate so only the current unscheduled reminder is incremented.
raw_findings.title: Retry increments lose updates during overlapping cron runs
raw_findings.trigger: Two overlapping scheduleSMSReminders invocations read the same unscheduled reminder and both encounter a scheduling failure before either update commits.

raw_findings.body: The second update rejection escapes the catch block, the handler rejects without sending its final response, and later reminders in the loop are not processed.
raw_findings.failure_mode: An error while recording a retry converts a recoverable per-reminder failure into a request-level cron failure.
raw_findings.impact: The second update rejection escapes the catch block, the handler rejects without sending its final response, and later reminders in the loop are not processed.
raw_findings.root_cause: The catch block added a potentially throwing database operation without protecting it from failure.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Wrap retry bookkeeping in its own try/catch, log bookkeeping failures, and allow the per-reminder loop to continue without rethrowing from the original error handler.
raw_findings.title: Retry bookkeeping failure aborts the SMS cron handler
raw_findings.trigger: Twilio or message-generation code throws for one reminder and the retryCount database update also throws, such as during a transient database outage or when the row was concurrently deleted.

raw_findings.body: The cron retries and can create multiple Twilio schedules, then deletes the database reminder when retryCount exceeds one without cancelling those already-created SMS messages, causing duplicate notifications and orphaned provider schedules.
raw_findings.failure_mode: External scheduling state and database retry state diverge, so cleanup removes the local record while provider-side messages remain active.
raw_findings.impact: The cron retries and can create multiple Twilio schedules, then deletes the database reminder when retryCount exceeds one without cancelling those already-created SMS messages, causing duplicate notifications and orphaned provider schedules.
raw_findings.root_cause: The catch path treats every exception as evidence that no SMS was scheduled, including exceptions from persisting the result after Twilio already accepted it.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Make provider scheduling and reminder persistence idempotent, or track whether Twilio returned a SID and reconcile or cancel that SID instead of counting a post-acceptance persistence error as a send failure.
raw_findings.title: A successful Twilio schedule can be orphaned by retry cleanup
raw_findings.trigger: Twilio accepts the scheduled SMS, but the subsequent update that sets scheduled: true and stores the SID fails; the same persistence failure occurs on two later scheduling attempts.

finding.title: Retry increments lose updates during overlapping cron runs
finding.trigger: Two overlapping scheduleSMSReminders invocations read the same unscheduled reminder and both encounter a scheduling failure before either update commits.
finding.verifier_reason: Patch lines 184 and 195 show `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value read at findMany time. If two cron invocations overlap and both read the same reminder with retryCount=0, both will write retryCount=1, losing one increment. This is a classic read-modify-write race. The trigger (overlapping cron runs) is plausible for a 15-minute cron schedule.

finding.title: A successful Twilio schedule can be orphaned by retry cleanup
finding.trigger: Twilio accepts the scheduled SMS, but the subsequent update that sets scheduled: true and stores the SID fails; the same persistence failure occurs on two later scheduling attempts.
finding.verifier_reason: The claim requires Twilio to accept the SMS and then the subsequent update to fail, with this happening twice to reach retryCount > 1. However, the code structure shows that if scheduledSMS is truthy (Twilio accepted), the update sets scheduled: true. The catch block only runs on exceptions, not on successful Twilio calls. The scenario described conflates different code paths and the evidence doesn't support that a successful Twilio schedule leads to retry increment.
